text:
alex: FYI I dropped an early implementation of a "access microgateway" that performs auth pre-fanout and returns a compact signed permit token for downstream workers. looking for quick feedback on tradeoffs.

tori: nice. main Q: how big are those tokens and how often will workers fetch them?

alex: token is ~160 bytes (HMAC-SHA256 over small payload), default ttl 8s. workers will prefer local LRU reuse keyed by (tenant, route, policy_v).

deep: sounds reasonable. worried about cold cache when dashboards fan out to 200 shards — that's 200 token checks. can we do a bulk-check API?
alex: added POST /auth/v1/batch in the prototype. accepts list of {tenant, route} and returns route->token map. internal batching coalesces DB reads.

liam: how do we handle policy updates? we cannot let stale tokens allow access after a deny rule is added.
tori: two patterns: embed policy_version in token and let workers compare to the gateway's latest version on mismatch, or short TTL + pubsub invalidations. both have tradeoffs.

alex: prototype uses policy_version in token. workflow: token = {allow:true, pv:123, exp:ts, sig:...}. worker checks pv vs local pv; on mismatch, revalidate via gateway.

deep: revalidate roundtrip could be expensive during rollout, but mismatches should be rare if we bump versions atomically. add metrics for revalidations.

liam: signing keys for hosted vs private deployments? on-prem needs KMS/HSM handling + rotation plan. ops should generate a key rotation doc.
tori: agreed. also consider supporting asymmetric signatures (ed25519) later for cross-cluster verification.

alex: noted. security: tokens short-lived (8s) and HMAC signed; workers verify signature. we also provide /introspect endpoint for debug but guarded by ops role.

deploy-bot: canary: deploy 0cfa9d passed smoke tests. gateway CPU under synthetic load ~6%.

deep: fallback behavior if gateway becomes unhealthy? deny-by-default is safest but risky for user-facing dashboards. propose per-route fallback policy with three modes: deny, allow-audit, degrade-with-cache.

liam: agree. add config like: ```json
{"routes": {"dash.read":{"fallback":"deny","cache_ms":400},"metrics.ping":{"fallback":"allow-audit","cache_ms":2000}}}
```

tori: also add a circuit-breaker threshold and an emergency-mode that extends token TTL to reduce pressure during gateway spikes. document SLO impact.
alex: will add SLO appendix. tentative p99 delta target when gateway enabled: +10ms. will run microbench and tenancy scalebench to validate.

deep: cache design: shared global LRU vs per-tenant partitions. shared is simpler but noisy-tenant risk. per-tenant bounded caches prevent noisy neighbor blowup but add more bookkeeping. we should prototype a hybrid: shared LRU with per-tenant soft quotas and eviction counters.

liam: add metrics: per-tenant eviction rate, token miss rate, batch hit ratio, revalidation rate, gateway latency p50/p95/p99. ops needs alerts for eviction spikes.
tori: we also need a test harness for policy rollouts: simulate policy changes and ensure workers observe invalidations within X seconds and no unintended allows. include integration test in the release pipeline.

alex: agreed. next actions: 1) update PR with per-route fallback config and circuit-breaker params, 2) add eviction metrics and tenant tags, 3) add e2e policy-rollout test, 4) schedule arch sync to decide KMS rotation strategy for private deployments.

deep: minor: consider compressing tokens for high-fanout responses (zlib) and use chunked transfer when returning large batch responses.

liam: also check header propagation and that proxies won't drop large auth headers; if so switch to attaching tokens in request metadata instead of headers.

alex: good call. I'll validate with ingress/sidecar config. thanks all, will iterate and request a short arch review tomorrow. :thumbsup:
